title: WCAG conformance target, scope and status
status_rationale: No Unbound user interface, conformance evaluation, ACR or accessibility test result exists as of 2026-11-25. Forma, the intended design system, has accessibility contracts and a pilot conformance test suite in its own repository (forma@c8f40b4c).
target_answer: Unbound conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA (which also satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA and 2.0 AA) on every surface and role: donor, advisor, successor, sponsor staff, administrator, charity and embedded partner widgets, on supported mobile and desktop platforms. Complex accounting workbenches may be desktop-optimized but remain conformant with reflow. Third-party embedded components are in scope and either conform or are documented exceptions with alternatives. Session timeouts warn users and allow extension except where a financial-security limit applies, and that limit is disclosed. The claim names the evaluation it rests on and is updated on material change. Conformance is achieved in the code and components themselves; Echelon does not use accessibility overlays or automated remediation widgets.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-PLAT-005 and CNV-EXP-001 set WCAG 2.2 AA as the requirement; no product exists to evaluate.
intended_practice: Evaluate each surface before activation under the activation gate.
provable: Nothing for Unbound. Forma has pilot conformance tests for its own components.
customer_statement: Unbound has no user interface yet, so we make no conformance claim. Our requirement is WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every surface, verified before activation.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: VPAT and Accessibility Conformance Report
status_rationale: No Unbound user interface, conformance evaluation, ACR or accessibility test result exists as of 2026-11-25. Forma, the intended design system, has accessibility contracts and a pilot conformance test suite in its own repository (forma@c8f40b4c).
target_answer: A current ACR in the ITI VPAT INT edition covers WCAG 2.2, the Revised Section 508 Standards and EN 301 549, is tied to a product version, states the evaluation methods and AT used, and is updated for each major release. The ACR is derived from continuously generated test evidence rather than a one-time audit, and an independent third-party evaluation validates it at least annually for customers who require it. Customers are notified when conformance changes.
intended_practice: Produce the first ACR when the first surface is ready for activation.
customer_statement: We do not yet have a VPAT or Accessibility Conformance Report because no product user interface exists. We plan to publish one before release.

title: Accessibility testing methodology
status_rationale: No Unbound user interface, conformance evaluation, ACR or accessibility test result exists as of 2026-11-25. Forma, the intended design system, has accessibility contracts and a pilot conformance test suite in its own repository (forma@c8f40b4c).
target_answer: Testing combines automated rule checks on every build (blocking regressions), layout checks at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 CSS px with 200 percent text and text spacing, forced-colors and reduced-motion checks, keyboard-only walkthroughs, screen-reader testing on named AT and browser pairs across desktop and mobile, and moderated usability sessions with disabled participants for essential journeys. AI agents that generate UI code are subject to the same gates; generated changes cannot merge without passing them and human review. Designers, engineers and support staff receive role-specific accessibility training.
current_practice: Not established for Unbound. Forma runs a blocking ui-conformance CI job (Chromium only) with layout, text-scale and action-outcome tests and axe checks in pilot fixtures; it reports pass, fail and unknown separately and does not claim catalog-wide conformance.
intended_practice: Adopt Forma's conformance helpers in the Unbound pipeline and add manual and AT testing.
provable: Forma's CI produces automated results for Forma components in Chromium; nothing for Unbound.
customer_statement: No Unbound accessibility testing has occurred because no interface exists. Our requirements call for automated, manual, screen-reader and disabled-user testing for every essential journey.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure accessibility is tested credibly, not just claimed.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Inaccessible journeys ship and are found by users or plaintiffs.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Periodic third-party audits find many issues but are snapshots; regressions reappear between audits, and automated scanners alone miss most failures.
challenge.legally_required: No method is legally required; the DOJ Title II rule sets WCAG 2.1 AA as the outcome for public entities.
challenge.contractually_required: Public-sector buyers sometimes require third-party audits.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partly: design-system components with contractual semantics, focus and contrast eliminate whole classes of failure for applications that use them correctly.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Blocking CI checks prevent automatically detectable regressions.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Component contracts plus blocking automation plus targeted AT testing, with periodic independent audit as validation rather than the primary control.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If application code bypasses design-system components or AT testing is skipped under schedule pressure.
challenge.alternative_risks: Chromium-only automation misses browser-specific failures; Forma lists Firefox and WebKit evidence as remaining work.
supporting_arguments: agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely if an independent audit is also offered.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Real users with disabilities find issues automation and internal testers miss.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Accessible documents, exports and communications
status_rationale: No Unbound user interface, conformance evaluation, ACR or accessibility test result exists as of 2026-11-25. Forma, the intended design system, has accessibility contracts and a pilot conformance test suite in its own repository (forma@c8f40b4c).
target_answer: Every issued document (statements, contribution acknowledgments, grant letters, reports) is available at issuance as accessible HTML generated from the same data snapshot with the same integrity reference, and any PDF is tagged and validated against PDF/UA-1 before release. Charts carry text or table alternatives; data exports are structured with headers; email templates pass accessibility checks with plain-text alternatives. Documents uploaded by sponsors or charities are outside Echelon's control; Echelon flags inaccessible uploads and the allocation of responsibility is stated in the contract.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-RCN-PLT-010 and CNV-EXP-001 AC-4 require accessible renditions and PDF/UA-1 validation. Folio provides print markup and preserves reading order by requirement, but tagged PDF and PDF/UA are explicitly not assumed (folio@56a18e1:docs/requirements/unbound-financial-report-consumer-capability-review-2026-11-23.md); CNV-EXP-001 states the PDF pipeline is Unbound-owned until an upstream renderer exists.
intended_practice: Run the rendering spike (RCD-009 DG-04) to confirm accessible HTML and a PDF/UA-capable pipeline before statements launch.
customer_statement: We do not yet produce documents. Our requirements call for an accessible HTML version of every document and validated tagged PDFs; the PDF accessibility pipeline has not been selected or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure disabled donors and staff can read statements, receipts and reports.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Blind donor cannot read a tax acknowledgment; discrimination complaint.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Buyers ask for 'accessible PDFs'; tagged PDF generation from browsers is inconsistent and PDF/UA conformance is hard to achieve and verify, so claims are often unreliable.
challenge.legally_required: For public-entity customers, the DOJ Title II rule covers conventional electronic documents with limited exceptions; for others, depends on ADA Title III interpretation.
challenge.historical_convention: PDF as the document of record.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partly: generating accessible HTML from the same snapshot as the PDF means the accessible version is never an afterthought and is provably the same content.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Issuance gate requires both renditions and PDF validation.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Accessible HTML as a co-equal rendition of record, with PDF/UA where achievable.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by snapshot identifier and validator output.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If the PDF is the only legally recognized record for a use and cannot be made PDF/UA conformant.
challenge.alternative_risks: Automated PDF/UA validators cannot check all Matterhorn conditions; manual review is still needed.
supporting_arguments: HTML is more reliably accessible than PDF across AT.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: some recipients require PDF specifically.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Two renditions double the testing surface.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Design-system accessibility contracts and branding
status_rationale: Forma's accessibility contracts exist and are partially tested in Forma's own repository (pilot), but no Unbound product consumes them yet.
target_answer: Unbound builds all interface elements from Forma components whose semantics, focus visibility, contrast-gated color roles, forced-colors behavior, reflow at 320 CSS px and target sizes are contractually specified and tested in the design system, so applications inherit them. Sponsor branding is compiled through a contrast gate that fails any non-conforming color pair, so white-labeling cannot reduce accessibility. Each Forma component used is pinned by release digest and covered by a conformance statement or an Unbound contract test.
current_practice: Forma (forma@c8f40b4c) is a zero-runtime CSS design system with accessibility contracts: status foregrounds contrast-gated at 4.5:1, forced-colors projection to system colors, a blocking Chromium-only ui-conformance CI job, and catalog requirements for 320/390 px, 200 percent text, reduced motion and WCAG 2.2 A/AA. Status is implementation pilot, not a passed release gate. Unbound does not yet consume Forma.
intended_practice: Consume Forma in Unbound with pinned versions and contract tests; implement sponsor brand compilation with the contrast gate.
provable: Forma repository test results for Forma components only. Nothing for Unbound.
customer_statement: Our intended design system, Forma, specifies accessibility contracts for its components and is in a pilot testing phase. Unbound does not yet use it in a released product.

title: Accessibility legal obligations and contract terms
status_rationale: No legal applicability assessment exists; UNB-GAP-031 calls for ADA obligations to be assessed separately and UNB-PLAT-005 notes automated WCAG checks do not establish ADA compliance. The DOJ Title II web rule compliance dates were extended by interim final rule (effective 2026-04-20) to 2027-04-26 for public entities of 50,000 or more population and 2028-04-26 for smaller entities (SRC-ADA).
target_answer: Echelon has a counsel-reviewed assessment of which accessibility laws apply by customer segment: the DOJ ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA for state and local government web content and mobile apps, including content provided through contractors) for public-entity customers such as public universities; ADA Title III exposure for sponsors serving the public; Section 508 for any federal agency buyer; state accessibility laws; and the European Accessibility Act only if Echelon provides in-scope services to EU consumers. Contracts include an accessibility warranty to WCAG 2.2 AA with remediation commitments; indemnity is negotiated case by case.
intended_practice: Commission the applicability assessment before selling to public-sector or EU customers.
customer_statement: We have not yet completed a legal assessment of accessibility obligations. We will provide one, with contract terms, before contracting with public-sector or EU customers.
owner: Proposed: General Counsel (role not yet staffed)

title: Accessible authentication, verification, timeouts and support
status_rationale: No Unbound user interface, conformance evaluation, ACR or accessibility test result exists as of 2026-11-25. Forma, the intended design system, has accessibility contracts and a pilot conformance test suite in its own repository (forma@c8f40b4c).
target_answer: Every identity-verification and step-up path has an accessible alternative reaching the same assurance level (mailed one-time code, outbound call to a verified number, captioned assisted video, in-person or notarized verification), relay calls are accepted at the same assurance as voice, and authentication does not require a cognitive function test without an alternative. Session timeouts warn and allow extension except where a disclosed security limit applies. Support channels and documentation meet Section 508 Chapter 6 and EN 301 549 clause 12 expectations, and accommodation requests never presume incapacity.
current_practice: Not established. CNV-PLT-011 specifies the AccessibleAssurancePath; ADM-045 requires accommodation without assuming incapacity.
intended_practice: Build accessible assurance paths with the identity and contact-change features.
customer_statement: Our requirements include accessible alternatives for identity verification and support, including relay calls. Not yet built.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)
